subject: Pilot model slate & TPS anchors — next steps + regression watchlist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot model slate & TPS anchors — next steps + regression watchlist

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and a suggested pilot slate so your engineering team can validate both latency/TPS and quality tradeoffs at short notice. I kept the list focused based on your constraints (multi-turn context ~1k tokens, typical response length ~120 tokens, hard 200 ms median latency target for UI flows).

Recommended pilot slate (Redwood-verified performance anchors):
- Redwood-Gen-13B-int8 (recommended start) — steady TPS anchor: 28 rps on A100(80GB), p50 latency 90 ms, p95 latency 240 ms. Good quality for instruction templates and summarization.
- Redwood-Instruct-30B-q4f — steady TPS anchor: 11 rps on A100, p50 170 ms, p95 420 ms. Higher quality on retrieval-augmented prompts; cost/latency tradeoff vs 13B.
- Redwood-Redwood-70B-4bit (batched) — steady TPS anchor: 4.5 rps on A100, p50 420 ms, p95 980 ms. Use only if you need highest fidelity for complex reasoning.

Why these anchors: we surface steady TPS (tokens/sec steady-state for a 120-token reply workload) rather than peak token throughput to reflect production behaviour under continuous small requests. "TPS anchors" give you predictable cost/backpressure tradeoffs for autoscaling. Full profile CSV attached (redwood_tps_profiles_parallax.csv).

Quality / regression watchlist:
- Quantization checks: we recommend A/Bing q4f vs int8 for the most-likely failure modes (numeric extraction, date normalization).
- Golden prompts: we provide a 30-example prompt set (attached: parallax_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl) for early regression detection.
- Eval harness: we propose running our small harness (unit: 500 synthetic+150 golden) nightly during the pilot; see checklist attached. Marcus added a few notes below on automatic alerting.

Links & next steps:
- Full perf profiles and raw traces: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/PX-4782/profiles
- If you can confirm which model(s) you want in the 14-day pilot, we can spin a dedicated sandbox (no production keys) and share a DocuSign pilot agreement.

Action items for Parallax: confirm pilot model(s) and preferred start window (we typically need 48 hours to provision the sandbox).

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick tech call with your infra lead if helpful.

— Olga

Subject: Re: Pilot model slate & TPS anchors — next steps + regression watchlist

Thanks, Olga — super helpful. A few quick clarifications from my side before we confirm the pilot models: 

1) For the 13B-int8 anchor: can you share a short example of the prompt/response behavior where int8 shows degradation vs q4f? Our legal team is worried about hallucination differences if we move to heavier quantization.
2) For the 70B option: the p95 on that looks high (980 ms) — in practice would that push us over our UI timeout SLAs? We have a fallback path that can show a cached short answer, but want to understand failover behavior.
3) Who on your side will own the nightly regression alerts? We need someone to be the on-call contact for the pilot window.

Also: we need a very small NDAsigned before sharing any customer examples — do you have a standard one we can sign quickly? If possible we’d like the sandbox to include a seeded dataset of 500 anonymized queries so we can validate retrieval-AUG performance.

Happy to do the pilot next week if those items are clarified and we get the NDA.

— Maya
Head of Product, Parallax AI
maya@parallax.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot model slate & TPS anchors — next steps + regression watchlist

Thanks Maya — quick answers and an ops plan from our side.

1) Int8 vs q4f quality differences (short):
- Typical regressions with int8: tokenization edge-cases around dates, smaller numeric tables, and multi-step extraction. We see the highest delta on examples that require precise numeral formatting.
- Mitigation: run two-pass A/B (int8 vs q4f) during the pilot for a small golden set; if regression rate > 3% on the golden set we failover to q4f automatically. We can wire that into your Canary flow.

2) 70B p95 and UI timeouts:
- The 980 ms p95 was measured under 8-request batching; single-request p95 often drops ~20–30% depending on request shaping. If you need strict p95 < 700 ms for UI, stick to 13B or q4f 30B for the production path and reserve 70B for async or background tasks.

3) Nightly regression alerts & ownership:
- We'll provision a PagerDuty escalation to your SRE alias and assign a Redwood runbook owner (Aditya) for the pilot. He will subscribe the pilot to our regression pipeline and notify via the HubSpot deal channel when thresholds are breached.

Attachments I am including: a short checklist for the eval harness and a zipped sample of latency traces we referenced (latency_traces_20261128.zip).

Proposed pilot schedule: start Wed Dec 8 (2 weeks), initial guardrails enabled (golden set + nightly runs) and a mid-pilot sync in week 1. If that works, Olga can send the DocuSign and we’ll provision sandbox infra.

— Marcus
